free_tier.stated: Free account: up to 50k lookups per month, as the pricing page states; the home page says the product is joining ipstack.com and sends sign-ups there, and api.iptrace.io does not accept connections.
free_tier.notes: The pricing page also lists paid plans from USD 8 a month, billed as USD 100 a year, for 200k requests a month.

interface_detail: GET https://api.iptrace.io/ip/{ip}/json?apikey=KEY, JSON with country, city, region, coordinates, time zone, ISP and country details; the host does not accept connections on ports 443 and…
chaining: Not reachable: the API host times out and the home page sends sign-ups to ipstack.com, which has its own record (data-apis/ipstack). Bulk path: none stated

limits.value: 50k lookups a month on the free account, as listed on the pricing page

binding_note: The API host accepts no connections, so no quota can be used; the listed 50k a month is the only stated limit.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the sign-up page answers HTTP 404 and the home page sends sign-ups to ipstack.com; an account was needed for an API key, and the home page says no credit card is required

reliability_note: api.iptrace.io does not accept TCP connections on ports 443 and 80 (20-second timeouts) while iptrace.io answers; the ipstack notice is on the home page in every archived copy from 2019-08-23 on.
confidence_note: The home, pricing and documentation pages and archived copies of 2019, 2025 and 2026 were read on 2026-11-02, and the API host's connection timeouts were measured; no keyed request was possible. A working api.iptrace.io would reopen the verdict.
